findings.title: Embedded-post username link lightness changed from 30% to 70% (should be 30/70 pair)
findings.body: In `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the light-theme value identical and adds the complementary dark-theme value (primary X% / secondary 100-X%), e.g. the matching rule for `.names span a` in common/base/topic-post.scss uses 30%/70%. Here the primary lightness was silently changed from 30% to 70%, so in light themes the embedded-post author link becomes much lighter than before, and the pair is not complementary. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

findings.title: Mobile .custom-message-length primary lightness changed from 70% to 30%, diverging from desktop
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` in mobile/modal.scss was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop counterpart in desktop/modal.scss (same selector, changed in this PR) uses 70%/30%. The mobile change therefore alters the light-theme color of the flag message character-count hint from a 70% lightness tint to a 30% tint (much darker), which is both a light-theme visual regression and an inconsistency with desktop. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)`.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map h3 lightness changed from 20% to 50%, diverging from desktop
findings.body: The `.topic-map h3` color in mobile/topic-post.scss was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The equivalent rule in desktop/topic-post.scss (also changed in this PR) uses 20%/80%. The mobile change silently alters the light-theme heading color of the topic map summary (e.g. "Topic Summary" / participants headers) from a near-full-strength color to a 50% tint, and the pair is not complementary. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)`.

findings.title: group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% instead of 30/70 pair
findings.body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` (desktop/user.scss), the color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The conversion pattern used everywhere else in this PR (and for the analogous `.username a` rule in common/base/user.scss, which correctly uses 30%/70%) preserves the light-theme value. Here the primary lightness was changed from 30% to 50%, lightening the group-member name in light themes and making the pair non-complementary. It should be `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)`.

findings.title: Mobile group-member-info .name lightness changed from 30% to 50% instead of 30/70 pair
findings.body: In `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` (mobile/user.scss), the color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. As with the desktop counterpart changed in this PR, the light-theme value was silently altered from a 30% tint to a 50% tint and the primary/secondary lightness pair is not complementary (correct form is 30%/70%, matching `.username a` in common/base/user.scss). This changes the visible color of group-member names in light themes on mobile.
